summary: Log repeatedly prints the message "Ticking entity", and finally crashes the game
description: The bug I m just moving around in my jungle world while trying to record a youtube video. Windows that were open are chrome, obs, sticky notes, streamlabs obs, and the minecraft launcher, as well as the game The game will crash after moving around a little bit. Very lagging in the jungle, the log repeatedly prints the message "Ticking entity", and finally crashes the game. Reproduce - Create a superflat world of jungle biome, and fly freely on the world. minecraft:bedrock,63 minecraft:dirt,minecraft:grass_block;minecraft:jungle;biome_1,decoration,lake,lava_lake - Using spawn eggs to spawn very many parrots. - Use the following command /tp @e[type=parrot] @p Here is the crash report: 19w40a: [^crash-2019-10-03_23.59.03-client.txt] Description: Ticking entity java.lang.NullPointerException: Ticking entity at atd.a(SourceFile:407) at akm.ab(SourceFile:301) at akn.ab(SourceFile:228) at akd.h(SourceFile:399) at akm.h(SourceFile:2059) at akn.h(SourceFile:295) at atk.h(SourceFile:34) at dmr.a(SourceFile:165) at bjk.a(SourceFile:648) at dmr.g(SourceFile:136) at das.n(SourceFile:1389) at das.d(SourceFile:907) at das.b(SourceFile:569) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Create a new superflat world with the following settings: `minecraft:bedrock,63 minecraft:dirt,minecraft:grass_block;minecraft:jungle;biome_1,decoration,lake,lava_lake`.
2. Ensure you have spawn eggs for parrots in your inventory.
3. Use the spawn eggs to spawn a large number of parrots in the world.
4. Execute the command `/tp @e[type=parrot] @p` to teleport all parrots to your location.
5. Move around freely within the jungle biome while monitoring the game's performance.
6. Observe that the log repeatedly prints "Ticking entity".
7. Continue moving until the game crashes, noting the crash message and any relevant details from the debug screen or logs.

8. Exit the game and gather the `debug` folder and `latest.log` file for further analysis.
Observed Behavior: When moving around in a jungle world while attempting to record a YouTube video, the game experiences significant lag and eventually crashes. The log repeatedly prints the message "Ticking entity" before the crash occurs. This issue can be reproduced by creating a superflat world with a jungle biome using the following seed: `minecraft:bedrock,63 minecraft:dirt,minecraft:grass_block;minecraft:jungle;biome_1,decoration,lake,lava_lake`. The problem is exacerbated when using spawn eggs to create numerous parrots and teleporting them near the player with the command `/tp @e[type=parrot] @p`. During these actions, the game becomes very laggy in the jungle environment. The crash report indicates a `NullPointerException` related to ticking an entity: `java.lang.NullPointerException: Ticking entity at atd.a(SourceFile:407)`. This bug occurs while other applications such as Chrome, OBS, Sticky Notes, Streamlabs OBS, and the Minecraft launcher are running simultaneously.
Expected Behavior: When moving around in a jungle biome with many parrots, the game should remain stable and not crash. The log should not repeatedly print "Ticking entity," and gameplay should be smooth without excessive lag. Parrots should behave normally and not cause any performance issues or crashes.
